acts.24.p1.b1.text: Five days later the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, who presented to the governor their case against Paul.

acts.24.p1.b2.text: When Paul had been called in, Tertullus opened the prosecution:

acts.24.p1.b3.text: “Because of you, we have enjoyed a lasting peace, and your foresight has brought improvements to this nation. In every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, we acknowledge this with all gratitude.”

acts.24.p1.b4.text: But in order not to burden you any further, I beg your indulgence to hear us briefly.

acts.24.p2.b5.text: We have found this man to be a pestilence, stirring up dissension among the Jews all over the world. He is a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,

acts.24.p2.b6.text: and he even tried to desecrate the temple; so we seized him.

acts.24.p2.b7.text: By examining him yourself, you will be able to learn the truth about all our charges against him.”

acts.24.p3.b9.text: When the governor motioned for Paul to speak,

acts.24.p3.b10.text: “Knowing that you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I gladly make my defense.”

acts.24.p3.b11.text: You can verify for yourself that no more than twelve days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship.

acts.24.p3.b12.text: Yet my accusers did not find me debating with anyone in the temple or riling up a crowd in the synagogues or in the city. Nor can they prove to you any of their charges against me.

acts.24.p4.b14.text: that I worship the God of our fathers according to the Way, which they call a sect.”

acts.24.p4.b15.text: and I have the same hope in God that they themselves cherish, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.

acts.24.p4.b16.text: In this hope, I strive always to maintain a clear conscience before God and man.

acts.24.p5.b17.text: After several years, then, I returned to Jerusalem to bring alms to my people and to present offerings.

acts.24.p5.b18.text: At the time they found me in the temple, I was ceremonially clean and was not inciting a crowd or an uproar. But there are some Jews from the province of Asia

acts.24.p5.b19.text: who ought to appear before you and bring charges, if they have anything against me.

acts.24.p5.b20.text: “It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.”

acts.24.p6.b21.text: Then Felix, who was well informed about the Way,

acts.24.p6.b22.text: “When Lysias the commander comes, I will decide your case.”

acts.24.p6.b23.text: He ordered the centurion to keep Paul under guard, but to allow him some freedom and permit his friends to minister to his needs.

acts.24.p7.b24.text: After several days, Felix returned with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess. He sent for Paul and listened to him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.

acts.24.p7.b25.text: As Paul expounded on righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment,

acts.24.p7.b27.text: “You may go for now. When I find the time, I will call for you.”

acts.24.p8.b28.text: At the same time, he was hoping that Paul would offer him a bribe.

acts.24.p8.b29.text: So he sent for Paul frequently and talked with him.

acts.24.p9.b31.text: Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. And wishing to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in prison.
